description:
# Auto-fill quantity from BOQ chainage when a BOQ item is selected in DPR entry

  ## What & Why
  When a user selects a BOQ item in the DPR progress entry form, the quantity field is left blank — the user must manually enter it. If the BOQ item has a chainage stretch (chainageFrom/chainageTo) in its work programme bar, the quantity could be auto-suggested as `stretch × multiplier` (same logic used in WorkProgramme.tsx).

  ## Done looks like
  - When a BOQ item is selected in SiteEntry.tsx or SiteEdit.tsx, if the item has a default quantity/multiplier in its work programme bar, pre-fill the quantity and UOM fields
  - A "suggested" indicator shows that the value was auto-filled; user can override freely
  - Uses calculateStretchQty from shared/planningEngine.ts

  ## Relevant files
  - `client/src/pages/SiteEntry.tsx` (lines ~780-821, the BOQ item select handler)
  - `client/src/pages/SiteEdit.tsx` (lines ~960-1032, same handler)
  - `shared/planningEngine.ts` (calculateStretchQty)
title: Auto-fill BOQ item quantity into the DPR quantity field based on chainage

description:

description:
# Show zero-quantity rows greyed out in Step 2

  The skip-zero-qty toggle was added to Step 3, but in Step 2 (category assignment) zero-qty rows still look identical to normal rows. Users assigning categories don't know which rows will be dropped. Greying them out with a "will be skipped" badge makes the wizard clearer.

title: Show zero-quantity rows visually greyed out in Step 2 so users know they'll be skipped

description:
# Persist import preferences across sessions

  ## What & Why

  ## Done looks like
  - Import mode and skip-zero-qty toggle are read from / written to localStorage on change
  - Values survive page refresh and re-opening the wizard
  - No migration needed — just a `useLocalStorage` or `localStorage.getItem` pattern in the existing state initialisers

  ## Relevant files
  - `client/src/components/BoqImportWizard.tsx` (lines 135–139 for the two state declarations)
title: Remember the last-used import settings so users don't have to re-pick them each time

description:
# Show which SNL items were rule-matched vs fuzzy-matched in the mapping panel

  ## What & Why
  After Patch 8G, BOQ items can be mapped via three methods: explicit SNL code, rule-based pre-match, or IDF-weighted fuzzy scoring. The `snlBoqMappings.mappedBy` column already stores "rule", "auto", or "auto-propagated". Surfacing this in the SNL panel gives engineers confidence in the quality of each mapping before accepting them.

  ## Done looks like
  - Each mapped item in the SNL panel shows a small badge: "rule", "fuzzy", "code", or "propagated" depending on mappedBy value
  - The mapped-items list (currently collapsed/not shown) is expanded to show at least the count with a breakdown tooltip
  - The mapped item list shows snlItemCode alongside the badge so engineers can spot wrong matches

  ## Relevant files
  - `client/src/pages/BoqProjectDetail.tsx` (SnlMappingPanel, lines 600-870)
  - `server/routes.ts` — the existing BOQ items endpoint that returns snlMappingStatus, snlItemCode, snlConfidence already passes these through
title: Show which SNL items were rule-matched vs fuzzy-matched in the mapping panel

description:
# Tune SNL auto-mapping thresholds based on real project mapping history

  ## What & Why
  The current CONFIDENT_FLOOR (0.10), CONFIDENT_MARGIN (1.30), and SUGGEST_FLOOR (0.04) were calibrated on a small synthetic corpus. Once a real project has been fully mapped (manually confirmed), those confirmed mappings become ground-truth training data that can be used to evaluate and tune the thresholds more accurately.

  ## Done looks like
  - An admin-only endpoint (GET /api/snl/mapping-stats) that returns: total mapped, rule-matched %, fuzzy-matched %, average confidence by tier, and count of manually-overridden auto mappings
  - The stats are shown on the SNL admin/seed page so admins can see how well auto-mapping performs on the current SNL corpus
  - Optionally: a threshold-tuning UI (two sliders: CONFIDENT_FLOOR and SUGGEST_FLOOR) with a preview of how many items would shift tier

  ## Relevant files
  - `server/snlAutoMapper.ts`
  - `server/routes.ts` (SNL section ~line 10305)
title: Tune SNL auto-mapping thresholds based on real project mapping history

description:

description:

  - `server/routes.ts` — add bulk endpoint near line 9615

description:
# Show structure-item demand separately in monthly tables

  ## What & Why
  Structure-type BOQ items (bridges, culverts, retaining walls) carry their full quantity at a fixed location, not distributed linearly across the road. Right now the "Structure" chip in the Materials tab flags these rows, but monthly columns still spread the quantity across the bar's duration using the same fractional-overlap logic as road items. A planner viewing "BC – Month 3: 450 MT" and "Deck Concrete – Month 3: 180 CUM" can't tell that the deck concrete must arrive at one chainage, not spread over 15 km.

  ## Done looks like
  - Structure-item demand in the Materials / Equipment / Labour monthly tables is marked with a light-violet background row or a dedicated "Structure items" subtable beneath each monthly column summary
  - Tooltip or footnote clarifies that structure quantities are point-concentrated (full qty in the bar's scheduled month range, not per-km)
  - The existing "Structure" chip (added in the current task) remains as the primary signal

  ## Relevant files
  - `client/src/pages/WorkDemand.tsx` — MaterialsTable, EquipmentTable, LabourTable
  - `shared/planningEngine.ts` — calculateBomDemand, calculateMonthlyDistribution
  - `client/src/pages/WorkProgramme.tsx` — StretchRow (structure qty input)
title: Show structure-item demand separately in monthly tables so planners aren't misled by linear distribution

description:
# Prevent planners from accidentally entering chainage ranges for bridge/culvert bars

  ## What & Why
  Structure-type items (bridges, culverts, box drains) exist at a single point on the road, not a chainage stretch. The Gantt bar dialog currently accepts chainageFrom–chainageTo for all items. For structure items it now shows a direct-qty input, but the chainage fields are still editable — a planner can enter "0–2 km" for a culvert that sits at ch. 1+200, making programme charts misleading.

  ## Done looks like
  - For structure items, chainageFrom is pre-filled to the item's design chainage (if known) and the chainageTo field is either hidden or locked to chainageFrom + a nominal 0.01 km span
  - A small hint text explains: "Chainage fixed at point location for structure items"
  - Alternatively, a single "Point chainage" field replaces the from/to pair for structure items in the bar add/edit dialog

  ## Relevant files
  - `client/src/pages/WorkProgramme.tsx` — StretchRow component (bar dialog, isStructure path)
  - `shared/schema.ts` — workProgramBars (chainageFrom, chainageTo fields)
title: Prevent planners from accidentally entering chainage ranges for bridge/culvert bars

description:

  - `shared/schema.ts` — WorkProgramBar type (planningWorkType carried through)
title: Let structure items in the Gantt show a point-location marker instead of a horizontal bar

description:

description:
# Extend composite layer detection to SDBC+DBM and other multi-layer combos

  - `server/routes.ts` lines 10040–10065 — `parseCompositeLayers` regex patterns
  - `client/src/pages/WorkDemand.tsx` — compositeLabel badge rendering
title: Extend composite layer detection to handle SDBC+DBM combinations in work programme BOM

description:
# Let planners manually override which front a structure or bridge is assigned to

  ## What & Why
  The auto-sequencer assigns culverts, drains, and bridges to fronts automatically based on chainage-group detection. On real projects planners often need to move a specific structure to a different front (e.g. a culvert that is physically close to Front 2 but contractually part of Front 3). Currently there is no way to do this without re-running the sequencer with different settings.

  ## Done looks like
  - Each BOQ item that gets auto-sequenced shows its assigned front label in the Gantt row header
  - A small "reassign front" action (inline or via right-click) lets the user pick a different front number
  - The override is stored on the BOQ item (e.g. a `sequenceFrontOverride` field) and respected on every future auto-sequence run
  - If the field is cleared, the auto-sequencer reverts to its automatic assignment

  ## Relevant files
  - `shared/programmeSequencer.ts` — sequencer logic, front assignment
  - `shared/schema.ts` — BOQ items table (add `sequenceFrontOverride` integer column)
  - `server/routes.ts` — auto-sequence endpoint (read override before assigning front)
  - `client/src/pages/WorkProgramme.tsx` — Gantt row rendering + override UI
title: Let planners manually override which front a structure or bridge is assigned to

description:
# Show a visual stage-completion indicator per front

  ## What & Why
  After sequencing, the Gantt shows bars grouped by front, but there's no at-a-glance way to see "Front 2 is on Stage 3 of 6". A compact progress indicator in the front-group header row (e.g. coloured dots or a mini step bar) would help site managers see how far each front has progressed without counting bars manually.

  ## Done looks like
  - Each "Road Front N" or "Struct. Front N" group header in the Gantt shows a small step indicator (e.g. ● ● ● ○ ○ ○ for stage 3/6)
  - Completed stages (bars whose end month ≤ today's month offset) are highlighted differently from future stages
  - Clicking the indicator collapses/expands that front's bars (already partially supported)

  ## Relevant files
  - `client/src/pages/WorkProgramme.tsx` — Gantt rendering, group-header rows
  - `shared/programmeSequencer.ts` — PAVEMENT_STAGE, CULVERT_STAGE, BRIDGE_STAGE constants (exported) used to determine max stages per track
title: Show a visual stage-completion indicator so planners can see progress through each front's construction sequence

description:
# Confirm auto-sequence correctness for mixed-track projects

  ## What & Why
  The sequencer was extended to handle three tracks (pavement, culvert/structure, bridge) in a single run. The existing tests cover pavement-only sequencing but there are no automated tests for:
  - A project with items from all three tracks in the same run
  - Bridge items being assigned to separate "Bridge Grp N" fronts rather than road fronts
  - Stage ordering (bridge stage 1 must always precede stage 2) when items are shuffled in the input array
  - staggerMonths and lagMonths being respected across all three tracks

  ## Done looks like
  - New test file (e.g. `tests/programmeSequencerMultiTrack.test.ts`) with at least 8 test cases covering the above scenarios
  - All existing 100 tests continue to pass

  ## Relevant files
  - `shared/programmeSequencer.ts`
  - `tests/` (add new test file alongside existing sequencer tests)
title: Confirm that auto-sequence handles mixed road+structure+bridge projects without scrambling bar order

description:
# Update existing BOQ items so Roadway Excavation gets the right equipment mix

  ## What & Why
  The new `roadway_excavation` WorkType has its own equipment recipe (excavator + grader, no compaction roller — because cutting doesn't need embankment-style compaction). However, existing BOQ items in the database that were previously classified as `earthwork` — including all "Roadway Excavation", "Excavation in Cutting" etc. items entered before this fix — still carry the old `earthwork` recipe (excavator + grader + vibratory roller + water tanker) in the `boq_item_equipment` table. Users who open those existing projects will see incorrect equipment on their cutting items until they manually trigger auto-build-recipes.

  A small DB migration or a one-time re-run of the auto-build step for items matching the new roadway_excavation classifier keywords would fix this silently.

  ## Done looks like
  - Existing BOQ items whose description matches the `roadway_excavation` classifier (e.g. "Roadway Excavation", "Excavation in Cutting", "Hill Cutting") automatically have their equipment rows updated to the new recipe on next server startup (or via a user-triggerable refresh button)
  - Items that don't match (plain embankment, GSB, etc.) are untouched
  - No manual re-run of auto-build-recipes required from the user

  ## Relevant files
  - `shared/workTypeRecipes.ts` — classifyWorkType + WORK_TYPE_RECIPES
  - `server/storage.ts` — buildBoqItemRecipes / upsertBoqItemEquipment
  - `server/routes.ts` — auto-build-recipes route (~POST /api/boq/projects/:id/build-recipes)
title: Update existing BOQ items so Roadway Excavation gets the right equipment mix

description:

For structures like culverts and bridges this looks cluttered — the same bridge may span three different BOQ items (foundations, walls, deck) and the user wants to see all its bars together under one heading row.

  - In `InlineGanttTable`, detect when any BOQ item has structure_location bars
  - Group those bars by `structureId` and render them under a collapsible "Structure Bars" section, showing structure ID + chainage as the group header
  - Normal stretch bars for the same item remain in their own "Road stretches" sub-section
  - Toggling the group hides/shows all bars for that structure

  ## Relevant files
  - `client/src/pages/WorkProgramme.tsx` — InlineGanttTable rendering (~line 1542)
  - `StructureLocationRow` component already built in same file
title: Show structure bars grouped by structure ID in the Gantt, not scattered inside each BOQ item section

description:

  - Queries all `planningMode = 'structure_location'` bars for the project
  - Writes an xlsx file with the same column layout as the import template (structure_id, chainage_km, boq_item_code, planned_qty, uom, start_date, duration_days, etc.)

  ## Relevant files
  - `client/src/pages/WorkProgramme.tsx` — toolbar area ~line 2402, StructureImportWizard already imports xlsx dynamically
  - `server/routes.ts` — or handle entirely client-side using xlsx
title: Let users export the structure schedule back to Excel from the Gantt (round-trip)

description:
# Expand MoRTH SDB norms — SDBC, Mastic Asphalt & more concrete grades

  ## What & Why
  The built-in MoRTH SDB seed covers 18 items (Chapters 2–7 core road works). Composite items like "BC + Mastic Asphalt + Prime Coat" now detect correctly, but Mastic Asphalt (5.14) only resolves because it was found in the AP SDB imports. A fresh deployment with only the MoRTH SDB seed will fail to rule-match the MASTIC_ASPHALT composite component to any SNL norm.

  Also missing: SDBC (Semi Dense Bituminous Concrete), BM with multiple thickness variants, PCC grades M15/M20/M30, RCC grades M30/M40, and general structure items.

  ## Done looks like
  - `shared/snlSeedData.ts` gains seed data for: Mastic Asphalt (5.14), SDBC, PCC M15/M20/M30, RCC M30/M40, and at least one RCC crash barrier norm
  - `seedSnlMorthSdb()` in storage.ts registers the new items
  - Composite composite-component rule-matching resolves Mastic Asphalt from the built-in seed without needing AP SDB imports

  ## Relevant files
  - `shared/snlSeedData.ts`
  - `server/storage.ts:21531-21605` — seedSnlMorthSdb()
  - `server/snlAutoMapper.ts:319-352` — COMPOSITE_PATTERNS (tag names must match seed itemCode patterns)
title: Expand MoRTH SDB norms so composites like mastic asphalt can be matched

description:

description:
# Show MoRTH norm details when browsing the SNL library

  ## What & Why
  The SNL library UI (NormsLibrary.tsx) currently shows items in a list with basic info. Now that MoRTH SDB items include structured labour, equipment, and material sub-rows, users should be able to expand an item and see its full norm breakdown (who, what, how much per shift).   - Clicking a norm item in the SNL library opens an expandable detail panel or drawer
  - Panel shows: productivity (shift output, output unit), labour rows (designation, qty/shift), equipment rows (label, hrs/shift), material rows (name, unit, qty/shift and derived per-unit)

  - `server/routes.ts` — GET /api/snl/items/:id already returns full detail

description:
# Prevent header-only items from being imported

  ## What & Why
  The MoRTH SDB parser currently saves 871 items that have ONLY a unit (no labour, equipment, or material sub-rows). These are intermediate hierarchy headers (e.g. "2.4 Dismantling of Structures" which is just a parent for 37 sub-variants). They clutter the auto-mapper's lookup pool and inflate the item count with useless entries.

  ## Done looks like
  - `parseChapterSheet` filters out items where `currentHasData = false` regardless of whether `current.unit` is set (current rule: save if has sub-rows OR has a unit)
  - After the change, imported item count drops from ~1,219 to ~348 (only real leaf items)
  - Existing seed items (18 hand-coded items) are unaffected

  ## Relevant files
  - `server/snlMorthParser.ts` — `finalise()` function (line ~200): change condition from `currentHasData || current.unit` to `currentHasData`
title: Prevent the MoRTH import from flooding the DB with 871 header-only items that have no norm data

description:

description:
# Prevent silent skips in bulk-auto-map when SNL corpus is empty

  ## What & Why
  snlAutoMapper.ts returns an empty result array when snlRows is empty, but routes.ts does not distinguish "no candidates found" from "no items to map". If the SNL data book has never been imported, the bulk-map API returns success with 0 mappings and no warning, leaving every BOQ item in "unmapped" state with no feedback.

  ## Done looks like
  - If snlRows.length === 0, the API returns a 400 or a clear JSON message: { skipped: N, reason: "SNL corpus is empty — please import the SNL data book first" }
  - The UI shows a toast with actionable text instead of silent 0/N mapped

  ## Relevant files
  - `server/snlAutoMapper.ts` — autoMapBoqItems()
  - `server/routes.ts` — POST /api/boq/projects/:id/snl-auto-map handler
title: Prevent SNL bulk-auto-map from silently skipping items when the corpus is empty

description:
# Sticky Column Header for BOQ Items Table

  ## What & Why
  Each CategorySection in BOQ Project Detail shows an items table (Item No., Description, Unit, BOQ Qty, Rate, Amount, Plan). When a category has many items (>10) the column header scrolls away while the category-section header stays pinned. description:
# Prevent silent no-op bugs when new bar-tracking fields are added

  ## What & Why
  The auto-sequence feature appeared broken in production because `storage.getWorkProgramBars()` in `server/storage.ts` uses an explicit Drizzle column select rather than `select()`. When the `stage`, `sequenceOrder`, `durationSource`, `needsReview`, and `scheduled` columns were added to the `workProgramBars` schema, they were never added to this select list, so every consumer of this function silently saw `undefined` for those fields. This caused the "unscheduled" scope filter in the auto-sequence endpoint to match zero rows with no error — the feature looked broken but was actually a data-plumbing gap. This class of bug (explicit selects silently dropping new columns) could recur for any future schema change touching `workProgramBars` or similar tables with hand-written selects.

  ## Done looks like
  - Audit other storage methods with explicit column selects (especially on `workProgramBars`, `boqItems`, and other frequently-extended tables) for the same missing-column risk.
  - Consider adding a lightweight test or lint check that fails when a table's Drizzle schema gains a column not present in its corresponding explicit-select storage method(s).

  ## Relevant files
  - `server/storage.ts` (getWorkProgramBars, and other explicit-select methods)
  - `shared/schema.ts` (workProgramBars table definition)
title: Prevent silent no-op bugs when new bar-tracking fields are added

# Prevent duplicate device approval requests when users retry quickly

  ## What & Why
  The latest device-login fix reuses a recently-pending device row when the same user retries from the same browser within 24 hours, which keeps admin inboxes tidy in the normal case. However, if the same user clicks "Login" two or three times in rapid succession (or tabs both reload at once), the pending lookup and insert are not atomic — two parallel login requests can each fail to find a pending row and each insert a fresh one. This still leaves admins seeing duplicate approval requests for the same browser.

  ## Done looks like
  - Two simultaneous login attempts from the same browser produce only one pending device row
  - Admins never see duplicate approval requests for a single login burst
  - No regression for normal sequential logins

  ## Relevant files
  - `server/auth.ts` (`ensureDeviceForUser`, branches 2b and 3)
  - `shared/schema.ts` (`userDevices` table — likely needs a partial unique index on `(userId, userAgent)` where `status='pending'`, or wrap the lookup+insert in a transaction with row locking)
title: Prevent duplicate device approval requests when users retry quickly

description:
# Add automated tests for the device login and approval flow

  ## What & Why
  The cross-user shared-browser login behavior has now had three rounds of subtle fixes (preserving the original user's cookie, allowing approved-device reuse on a trusted browser, blocking user-agent-only bypass on untrusted browsers, protecting bootstrap recovery from stale pending rows). The flow is critical for security but is currently only verified by manual click-through. A regression here can lock all users out or, worse, weaken authorization. A focused integration test suite would protect every future change to this code.

  ## Done looks like
  A test suite that covers, at minimum:
  - Same user, approved cookie → logs straight in, no cookie rotation
  - Same user, no cookie → goes through device approval
  - User X logging in on user Y's already-approved browser → returns pending, preserves Y's cookie, then claim-device flow rotates cookie after admin approval
  - User X already approved on this browser, logs in fresh → reuses approved row, rotates cookie
  - Untrusted browser (no cookie / pending cookie / revoked cookie) cannot bypass approval by spoofing the User-Agent header
  - Bootstrap admin recovery succeeds even when a stale pending or revoked device row exists for the same browser

  ## Relevant files
  - `server/auth.ts` (`ensureDeviceForUser`)
  - `server/auth-routes.ts` (`/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/device-status`, `/api/auth/claim-device`)
  - `client/src/pages/Login.tsx` (polling + claim flow)
title: Add automated tests for the device login and approval flow

description:
# Protect old shift-log data from being wiped by stale browsers

  ## What & Why
  The new "Boiler runs during production" toggle controls whether the boiler T1 opening/closing meter readings are saved or nulled on a Plant Shift Log. The current Plant Shift Log page has a back-compat guard (Task #254) that auto-flips the toggle ON when loading a legacy row that already has T1 readings, so editing such a row through the UI is safe. However, **a server-side guard is still missing**: any other client (a stale browser tab open before this fix shipped, a future API caller, an import script) could send `boilerRunsDuringProduction: 0` together with `ldoTank1OpeningMeter: null` / `ldoTank1ClosingMeter: null` on an existing row that has real T1 readings, and the server would silently overwrite them.

  ## Done looks like
  - The shift-log update path on the server refuses to overwrite an existing row's T1 opening/closing values with `null` unless the request is an explicit "clear" intent (e.g. the toggle was previously ON and the user just turned it OFF in this same submission).
  - A simple rule of thumb that's safe and easy to maintain: when toggle is OFF in the incoming payload, server reads the prior row; if prior `boilerRunsDuringProduction` was 1 OR prior had T1 values, the server keeps the prior T1 values unless the payload also includes an explicit `clearBoilerT1: true` flag (which the UI sets only when the operator turns the toggle from ON to OFF in that edit).
  - Manual smoke test: edit a legacy row with the new UI (toggle auto-flips ON), save, T1 values stay intact; toggle OFF and save, T1 values get cleared.

  ## Relevant files
  - `server/routes.ts` (Plant Shift Log create/update endpoints — search for `/api/plant-module/shift-logs`)
  - `server/storage.ts` (`upsertPlantShiftLog` / equivalent)
  - `client/src/pages/PlantShiftLog.tsx` (already has back-compat load-side guard at `legacyHasT1Reading`; add the explicit `clearBoilerT1` flag to the save payload only when the operator toggl...
title: Protect old shift-log data from being wiped by stale browsers

Today, those ledger rows are written once on creation but are not updated when the parent's opening/closing meter values are later corrected. Admins bypass all checks so they're unaffected, but engineers/managers will silently lose access until an admin re-grants it.

  A one-time startup migration that copies each user's `plant_stock` permissions into the new `plant_materials` slot (without touching existing plant_stock values) would prevent this disruption.

  ## Done looks like
  - A startup migration (similar to `backfillSplitPermissions` in `server/startup-tasks.ts`) runs once on startup.
  - For every user whose stored permission matrix has `plant_stock.view=true`, the migration sets `plant_materials.view=true` (and same for create/edit/delete/view_reports/export).
  - The migration is idempotent (skips users who already have any non-false `plant_materials` entry).
  - Migration is logged: "Copied plant_stock → plant_materials for N users".

  ## Relevant files
  - `server/startup-tasks.ts` (add new migration function)
  - `server/index.ts` (register the startup migration)
  - `server/storage.ts` (getAllUsers or similar to iterate users)

title: Auto-grant Material Receipts/Issues/Returns access to users who already had Stock access

# Stop dispatches from double-charging owners when HLC covers the shortage

  ## What & Why

Until it is, the double-deduction bug can silently recur on new dispatches, requiring manual data correction each time.

  ## Done looks like
  - Identify the specific code path in `createTruckDispatchWithStockDeduction` that produces both a non-zero owner row AND an HLC borrowed row for the same dispatch+material when the owner has no stock.
  - Add a guard: if `fromOwner === 0` and the HLC borrow branch is taken, the marker row for the owner must always have `quantity_out = 0` (it already does today for the *normal* path, but something is bypassing this).
  - Add a note or assertion that prevents the double-write from happening even if the code is refactored in the future.
  - No negative balances appear on any new dispatches created for parties that borrow from HLC.

description:
# Make the Ledger Rebuild tool work when HLC party is not named exactly 'HLC'

  ## What & Why
  Both the Dispatch Ledger Rebuild tool and the dispatch-creation code look up the HLC fallback party using `UPPER(TRIM(name)) = 'HLC'`. In production, the real HLC entity is named `'HIGH LANE CONSTRUCTIONS'` (party_id=1), so `hlcPartyId` resolves to `null` every time the rebuild runs. This means:
  - The rebuild never writes "Borrowed from HLC" rows (silently skips when hlcPartyId is null).
  - Orphan cleanup skips the HLC party entirely.
  - Any future dispatch for a non-HLC owner that needs HLC coverage also silently skips the borrow row.

  The fix should make the HLC lookup more flexible — e.g. matching any party whose name contains 'HLC' or 'HIGH LANE' (case-insensitive), or storing the HLC party_id as a configurable system setting.

  ## Done looks like
  - The HLC party is resolved correctly in production (party_id = 1 for HIGH LANE CONSTRUCTIONS).
  - Running the Ledger Rebuild tool on template 8 or 6 correctly writes "Borrowed from HLC" rows for dispatches where the owner's stock is zero.
  - The fix is applied to both the dispatch-creation path and the rebuild tool.
  - No regression on databases that DO have a party named exactly 'HLC'.

  ## Relevant files
  - `server/storage.ts:4037-4063` — HLC party lookup in `createTruckDispatchWithStockDeduction`.
  - `server/storage.ts:4388-4392` — HLC party lookup in `rebuildDispatchLedgerForTemplate`.
  - `server/storage.ts:4432` — `computeSplit` condition `dispatch.partyId === hlcPartyId` (can return wrong result when hlcPartyId=null).
title: Make the Ledger Rebuild tool work when HLC party is not named exactly 'HLC'

description:
# Split quantities correctly when LHS and RHS reaches have different chainage boundaries

## What & Why
The width-based LHS/RHS quantity split currently works only when both sides have IDENTICAL chainage boundaries. When an LHS stretch and an RHS stretch overlap but their boundaries differ (e.g. LHS 0–2 km, RHS 0.5–2 km), the app falls back to a flat 50/50 split with a note ("Width-based split needs matching LHS/RHS reach boundaries; using standard side allocation."). Segmented allocation — splitting by width only over the overlapping portion, full share over the one-sided remainder — would make planned quantities accurate for staggered side execution, which is common on widening projects.

## Done looks like
- A one-sided stretch overlapping its opposite side over part of its length gets a width-proportional share over the overlap and the full (0.5→appropriate) share elsewhere, computed per segment.
- The existing exact-match and no-overlap behaviours are unchanged.
- The fallback note disappears for cases the segmented math now handles.
- Unit tests cover partial-overlap, nested, and multi-segment cases.

## Relevant files
